codeReview.summary: The commit improves route behavior and adds strong scoped e2e coverage, but it does not actually complete the requested React migration: SettingsPage is a thin wrapper around the existing 2853-line vanilla settings renderer.

issues.description: Feature objective was to migrate settings.js into a React page, but the implementation imports and delegates to legacy settings.js (`settingsPage.render`) instead of implementing the settings UI in React. This leaves the core feature logic in vanilla DOM code and does not satisfy the migration requirement.

`disposeSettingsPage()` only nulls `settingsState.container` and does not clear draft/baseline state; combined with the 'discard changes' confirm flow in SettingsPage, users can navigate away after confirming discard yet return to find the unsaved draft still present.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission/skill guidance does not explicitly define what qualifies as a completed 'React migration' for a page; this allowed a legacy-wrapper implementation to pass worker validation for a migration feature.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: internal/channels/dashboard/ui/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:4 and :37 delegate to `./settings.js`, while the legacy implementation remains in internal/channels/dashboard/ui/src/pages/settings.js (2853+ lines).

sharedStateObservations.observation: The frontend-worker procedure's strict TDD-first step was explicitly deviated from in this feature; skill guidance should clarify acceptable exceptions for placeholder-to-parity migrations.

summary: Reviewed handoff, transcript skeleton, skill procedure, and commit 8c92e788. Despite passing scoped tests, the feature is marked FAIL because Settings was not truly migrated to React; the new page wraps legacy settings.js instead of replacing it with React-native implementation.
